chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The market of the Muslims is like their mosque. So whoever precedes to a place, he is more rightful to it until the night.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that he did not used to take rent for the market rooms (stalls)'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling regarding ownership or priority of spots in a public market?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s (AS) pragmatic approach to public space management, equating the sanctity and accessibility of markets with mosques to prevent monopolization. It underscores the principle of 'first-come, first-served' for temporary occupancy, reflecting a justice-oriented economic model where the state does not profit from basic commercial infrastructure, thereby ensuring equitable access for all merchants.
